items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1989-08-13
items.q: he would have been, uh, certainly acquainted with, uh, Oscar Celestan.

ctx.x: Uh-huh. What other kind of musical influences would Louis have heard growing up at Liberty and Perdita, or in that area? Uh-huh.

Well, he certainly would have heard whatever marching bands, parade bands were around. Uh-huh. And he would have been, uh, certainly acquainted with, uh, Oscar Celestan. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. And his music. And, uh, and I'm sure that he heard Bunk a lot in Olivier's band. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. And, uh, probably, uh, you know, he would have heard Tony Jackson, for instance.
Would he, would he have heard Tony? Yeah.

items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1975-02-03
items.q: my first recollection of Celestan comes from the time when I was about five years old, during which time he played in the house.

ctx.x: And did you go to hear music with him?

Uh, no, but he was the one who brought, who bought most of the records that came into the house. Mm-hm. And, uh, uh, of course we had all the early jazz records, largely because of the fact that he knew the musicians himself, and, uh, and I came to know many of the musicians when I was very young. I remember, for example, some social function that went on in the house when I was very young, for which Papa Celestan's band was hired. And, uh, while I don't remember who the individual musicians were, my first…
Well, was your uncle hiring bands?

items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1976-02-19
items.q: I mean, we'd hire Papa Celestan's band, you know. And so I knew all the musicians.

ctx.x: That's right. Yeah. Because, well, there was nothing else to take. And all those... See, there are a lot of musicians that the family just hired from time to time, like to go out to Millenburg for a picnic. I mean, we'd hire Papa Celestan's band, you know. And so I knew all the musicians. I've known, for example, Jeanette Kimball, who plays the piano in Papa Celestan's band. I've known her since I was five years old. And so, you know, having grown up with a musician like that, I mean, a musician was never…
